title: Drake and the Cimarrons on the Isthmus of Panama, 1572–73
summary: Drake sailed from Plymouth in May 1572 with two small ships to raid the Spanish treasure road across Panama. He attacked Nombre de Dios in July, was wounded, and withdrew. Escaped Africans, the Cimarrons, who hated the Spanish, then allied with him. They guided him inland, showed him the Pacific from a hilltop, and on 1 April 1573 helped him ambush a mule train carrying silver to the coast. He was back at Plymouth in August.

events.label: Nombre de Dios attacked
events.text: Drake's men landed at night and took the town, then withdrew when he was wounded in the leg, leaving the treasure house untouched.

events.label: The mule train ambushed
events.doubt: Drake's own account is the source for the amount taken and the place; the Cimarrons left no record.
events.text: Drake and the Cimarrons waited in the grass beside the road and took the silver of a mule train, and buried much of what they could not carry. The Cimarrons were in a war of their own with the Spanish; the Spanish suppressed them in the years after.
